summary.headline: EIH Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 10% but EBITDA up only 1% on business mix, wage code and higher expenses; FY26 PAT hit by Rs 30 Cr wage code charge.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a very volatile year (Operation Sindoor, West Asia conflict, monsoon rains, December flight disruptions, late-February West Asia war) but said EBITDA was the highest in company history. Q4 consolidated revenue grew 10% while EBITDA grew 1%, with profit from operations down 5% on higher tax expense, business mix shift toward lower-margin OFS (flight catering), higher airport levy, repair and maintenance, CSR, legal and donation costs. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 8% and EBITDA 3%; reported PAT fell on a one-time Rs 30 Cr wage code impact and the Mashobra fair-value charge from the prior year, and management said excluding these profit grew 2%. Management said April and May trends were better than expected, led by domestic demand.

Cash and funds balance, end FY26
financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,335 Cr vs Rs 1,051 Cr at end March 2025

segments.name: Oberoi hotels (luxury)
segments.commentary: Q4 RevPAR up 4.2% vs luxury segment 6%, dragged by Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up; FY26 RevPAR up 10.4% vs Indian luxury 6.4%. RGI 204 in Q4 and 191 for FY26, both above last year.

segments.name: Trident hotels (upper upscale)
segments.commentary: FY26 RevPAR up 10.2%, against 5% for the upper upscale segment, on both occupancy and ARR gains versus competition.

segments.name: International hotels
segments.commentary: Q4 RevPAR up 13%, with Mauritius, Oberoi Zahra and Sahl Hasheesh the main contributors.

segments.name: OFS (flight catering)
segments.commentary: Q4 business about Rs 145 Cr, driven mainly by existing airlines with larger flight counts and market share; this segment carries airport levy costs that weighed on margins.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give forward numbers; said April and May were better than expected, led by strong domestic demand.
Foreign business (about 50% of Q4 business historically) hit by West Asia war; management expects the impact to be limited in summer months, with foreign travel peaking October to March.
Management expects a big summit in Q2 and Q3 FY27 to benefit demand, following AI Summit benefit in February-March.
Capex of about Rs 600-700 Cr a year to continue for the next one to two years, rising in FY29-30 when larger hotels open.
Oberoi Grand Kolkata partial opening still targeted for September 2026; Trident Vizag opens 2027; 825 owned/associate keys and 1,893 managed keys in pipeline by 2030.
Mashobra hotel O&M continues until October 2026; management awaits further developments.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about Rs 680 Cr: about Rs 330 Cr on Mumbai land conversion (leasehold to freehold), Rs 125 Cr on Oberoi Rajgarh, about Rs 100 Cr on ongoing renovations (Kolkata and others), remainder replacement capex.
Oberoi Rajgarh opened November 2025, total 3,800 keys in business with Rajgarh added in Q3; about 400 international keys.

Pipeline: 825 owned/associate keys by 2030, starting with Trident Vizag (2027) via EIH Associated Hotels; Hebbal mixed-use site (about 1.3 million sq ft development, including about 7.6 lakh sq ft commercial) by 2030.
Managed pipeline: 24 hotels, 1,893 keys; two new Trident management contracts added (Amritsar, 150 keys; Pawna, 150 keys), signed between Q3 and Q4.

Oberoi Grand Kolkata (about 200 keys) renovation under way with structural works; reopening targeted September 2026. Oberoi Grand Kolkata cited as timeline issue; separately, Oberoi Gandikota site delay moved from 2028 to 2030 due to site change.

Renovations: about 90 rooms at Oberoi Bangalore in 18-room blocks over summer; Trident Nariman Point 4 floors (six months); 4 floors at Oberoi Mumbai one floor at a time; F&B overhaul at Trident Bandra Kurla later in FY27.
demand_pricing: Q4 industry occupancy 67-69%, below last year on West Asia war impact; industry ARR up 6-8% and RevPAR up 5-7%. FY26 industry occupancy flat, ARR up 9-10%, RevPAR up 10-12%.

Occupancy weakened through Q4 with a sharp drop in March; ARR for EIH owned hotels rose from Rs 24,548 to Rs 28,198 in Q4. January RevPAR negative (about -6%), which management attributed to unexplained weak demand, possibly negative international press on air quality.
Delhi/NCR, Mumbai (T20 World Cup) and Bhubaneswar grew strongly; Bangalore hit by lower foreign bookings; Udaipur down on fewer weddings.
Room revenue: MICE and direct segments grew; corporate and leisure flat.
Management says India is significantly underpriced versus Europe, North America and parts of Asia at the top end; no reason to discount rates given rate premium strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What drove February ARR growth near 25% and why was January RevPAR negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said January was weak, with promotions having limited effect; the likely cause (unvalidated) was negative international press on North India air quality. February was strong, helped by the AI Summit, deferred winter travel and strong demand across leisure and city hotels.

qa_highlights.question: With few owned key additions in FY27-28, what drives growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Two levers: ARR (premium positioning, headroom if market stays buoyant) and cost elimination of waste rather than cuts. No specific growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 flight catering (OFS) revenue and was it new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 145 Cr in Q4, mainly existing airlines expanding flights and market share, including some domestic airlines.

qa_highlights.question: Where do foreign tourist mix and Q4 FTA levels stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 foreign business about 50% historically; domestic share rose substantially in March and more than offset weaker foreign demand. Exact March quarter mix to be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a financial loss from geopolitical issues in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No financial impact calculated; lower foreign room nights were offset by domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 20% in Q4 and will Mashobra O&M continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher expenses from business growth, higher airport levy on OFS, higher R&M, CSR, legal and donation costs. Mashobra case settled in June; hotel operated until October 2026.

risks_watch: Margin pressure: Q4 EBITDA only 1% growth as OFS mix rises and airport levy and wage code costs increase; watch for margin recovery in FY27.
Managed hotel project slippage (Trident Goa, Dehradun, Rishikesh and others); management says owners control timelines and delays are not significant, but 2027 pipeline looks thin.
Oberoi Grand Kolkata renovation: structural issues found, reopening target September 2026 still stated; any change would be updated to the board and investors.
Oberoi Rajgarh (Khajuraho) connectivity: only seasonal Delhi flights; no flights expected July-September unless IndiGo extends.
Geopolitical risk: West Asia war impact on foreign travel and occupancy; the company has not quantified the impact; March occupancy weakness may persist into Q1 FY27.
Supply risk in FY29-30 from new luxury keys in some micro-markets; management says the rate premium will be maintained rather than discounted.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and pipeline but cautious on near-term occupancy; management acknowledged a challenging year and avoided forward numbers, deferring several specifics (foreign mix, flight catering split, consolidated room revenue) to offline follow-up.
